title: BTS Makes Historic Appearance at 52nd American Music Awards — First US Award Show in Four Years
detail: BTS makes their first US televised award show appearance in approximately four years at the 52nd American Music Awards, held at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas on May 25, 2026 (Memorial Day) — the same city as their ongoing ARIRANG World Tour residency at Allegiant Stadium. Hosted by Queen Latifah, the ceremony airs live on CBS. BTS holds three nominations: Artist of the Year (competing against Taylor Swift, Bad Bunny, Bruno Mars, Harry Styles, Justin Bieber, Kendrick Lamar, Lady Gaga, Morgan Wallen, and Sabrina Carpenter), Song of the Summer ('SWIM', competing against Harry Styles' 'American Girls' and Taylor Swift's 'Elizabeth Taylor'), and Best Male K-Pop Artist. Gold Derby and major entertainment outlets had BTS favored for Artist of the Year over Taylor Swift entering the ceremony. The convergence of the ARIRANG World Tour's Las Vegas residency and the AMAs — both at Las Vegas venues — makes May 25 a landmark day for BTS's long-awaited full return to the global stage. May 25 is a rest day between Tour Nights 2 (May 24) and 3 (May 27), with BTS making the AMAs their evening focus. The appearance marks the first time all seven members have attended a US awards ceremony together since their Permission to Dance on Stage era.

title: 'SWIM' Tops Billboard Global Excl. US for 6th Time in 2026 — Surpasses Taylor Swift's Annual Record
detail: In the chart cycle dated around May 25, 2026, BTS's 'SWIM' achieves its sixth No. 1 on the Billboard Global Excl. US chart in the 2026 calendar year — surpassing Taylor Swift's previous record for most No. 1 weeks on that chart in a single year. The milestone coincides with BTS's Las Vegas ARIRANG World Tour residency and their AMA appearance tonight at MGM Grand Garden Arena. 'SWIM' simultaneously sits at No. 2 on the Billboard Global 200 (its third consecutive week at No. 2) and No. 34 on the US Billboard Hot 100 — its eighth consecutive week on the US chart. The parent album 'ARIRANG' ranks at No. 8 on the Billboard 200, marking its ninth week on that chart. Starnews Korea reports that 'SWIM' has now logged more No. 1 chart weeks on Global Excl. US in a single year than any prior K-pop single. The track's resilience on global digital charts — driven by high streaming velocity across Latin America, Southeast Asia, Europe, and Oceania — underscores BTS's post-hiatus fandom engagement at levels analysts describe as exceeding pre-hiatus benchmarks.

media.caption: BTS 'SWIM' tops Billboard Global Excl. US for a 6th time in 2026, surpassing Taylor Swift's record for most annual No. 1 weeks on that chart
